article.title: Technical information
article.p: SaxonC is built by cross compiling the Java code of Saxon 12 using Graalvm native-image (version 22.3.0). This generates platform specific machine code, which we interface with C/C++ using the Native Image C API.

Embedded systems: It is also possible to build SaxonC for embedded systems, for example on a Linux/ARM System. If such a build is required please contact Saxonica to discuss further: support@saxonica.com.
The PHP interface is in the form of a C/C++ PHP extension to SaxonC created using the Zend module API. Supports PHP8.
The Python interface is in the form of a Cython module interfaced with the C/C++ SaxonC API. Currently supports Python3.
We currently use the Xerces XML parser which is also cross compiled. There are currently no links to libxml.
The following limitations apply to the 12 release:

ul.li: The ICU localization is currently not support in SaxonC-PE and SaxonC-EE.
The XQuery Update feature is not supported.
Host language extension functions is currently not supported in SaxonC 12.

article.p: Please use the help forums and bug trackers for SaxonC at saxonica.plan.io if you need help or advice. Or send email to support@saxonica.com.

section.title: Debugging
section.p: Exceptions and errors are captured and maintained silently in SaxonC, but can be accessed. This is due to the call-back mechanism of the Graalvm Native Image C API. We therefore catch handle any exception thrown in the Java code and report it in the C++ code as a SaxonApiException object.

Any exceptions or errors found in a SaxonC Processor class can be accessed by the getException() method which returns an SaxonApiException object. The method getMessage() indicates the underlying error message throw from the exception. It is also possdible to get the error message directly from the Processor objects too. For example, see the following PHP code snippet:
section.samp:
<?php
  ...
  $result = $query->runQueryToString();
  if($result == NULL) {
    if($query->exceptionOccurred()){
        $errC = $query->getErrorCode();
        $errMessage = $query->getErrorMessage();
        if($errC != NULL) {
          echo 'Error found: '. $errC.' :'.$errMessage;
        }
        $query->exceptionClear();
    }
  }
  ...
?>
